# P35.57 — API release parity (REL-05): release-backed routes serve the promoted release's files; live-spine routes disclose themselves

**Requirement ids:** **Owner (contract):** SIG-REL-010 (§56.6; G3 §6.4 /
REL-05) — every route whose answer the site shows serves the current promoted
release's files and names that release; every other route labels itself
`live-spine` with watermark + current release id; a promotion the API cannot
serve is refused. **Also cited:** SIG-TRANSP-025 (context; owned by P37.42 —
this row supplies the API-side parity it cites). **Ticket:**
`docs/tickets/261_P35.57__api-release-parity.md` (manifest row 261, Round 11 /
P35, sub-round 11B) · **Base:** `r11/P34.47-sub-round-11a-acceptance` ·
**Branch:** `r11/P35.57-api-release-parity` · **Gate:** the API-roll go was
collected at GATE-G4 §2 ("Grant the go now", recorded verbatim in GATE
DECISIONS 2026-10-09T17:32Z) · **Live stage:** production write (the `sig-api`
roll + the release-mount configuration) — **QUEUED, never executed:** the go
holds but the deployment prerequisites do not exist in this environment (no
`sig-api` service resolves, the Cloud Run/Compute APIs are disabled on the

**CI config changed:** no · **Size:** ~1.1k changed lines excl.
generated/fixtures — inside the M budget (≤3,000).

## Why

Until now every API answer came from the live claim spine, so the API and the
site could disagree: the site renders release-pinned bytes while the API
served newer spine state under a label that never named a release. G3 §6.4
(REL-05) splits the read surface into two declared basis classes —
release-backed routes answer the promoted release's own files; live-spine
routes keep serving the spine and disclose they are newer than the site — and
V7 refuses a promotion the API cannot serve.

## What ships

- **`api/src/api/release_serving.py` (new)** — `ReleaseServingStore`: verified
  read-only serving of the release's `r/<pub>/api/` slice
  (`sig.api-slice/1`). `?release=<publication_id>` selects any promoted
  release; the current pointer (`latest.json`) is the default. Every file is
  digest-pinned to the release's integrity manifest before it is served;
  withdrawals are re-evaluated per request (`route_access` — the same barrier
  P32.5 policy uses); a document whose embedded `release` block names a
  different publication fails closed. Refusals are typed
  `{detail, code}` errors: `unknown_publication`/`scope_not_available` (404),
  `withdrawn` (410), `release_artifact_absent`/`release_artifact_unpinned`/
  `release_verification_failed`/`release_metadata_mismatch`/
  `no_current_release` (503). No silent fall-back to the spine on a mounted
  registry, no placeholders (DR-C3-12 / ACT-08).
- **Route re-classification (`api/src/api/routes.py`)** — release-backed:
  `/v1/dossier/{scope}`, `/v1/coverage/{scope}`, `/v1/export`, `/v1/changes`,
  `/v1/sources`, `/v1/sources/{id}` (new routes; the J3/TX-15 copy is
  P37.23's), `/v1/releases` + `/v1/releases/latest` +
  `/v1/releases/{publication_id}`. Live-spine (description-stamped "newer than
  the site; not a citation"): `/v1/resolution`, `/v1/entity`, `/v1/claim`,
  `/v1/evidence`, `/v1/contradiction`, `/v1/task`, `/v1/crosswalk`,
  `/v1/search`. `/v1/changes?since=` filters the release snapshot's events
  exactly as it filters the spine's. When no registry is mounted the
  dossier/coverage/export/changes routes keep today's live-spine answers
  (additive back-compat); the registry-only routes answer an honest
  `503 release_serving_unconfigured`.
- **Dual basis (`api/src/api/basis_middleware.py`)** — handlers mark the
  request (`sig_basis` + `sig_release` in `scope["state"]`) *before* serving,
  so error bodies are labelled by the authority that answered. Release
  responses carry `X-SIG-Basis: release`, `X-SIG-Release: <label> <pub>`
  (G3 §6.3), `X-SIG-Basis-Release: <pub>` and body
  `basis {kind: "release", release: {…}}`. Live-spine responses keep the
  P34.25 wire keys (`type`, `watermark`, `release_id`) and gain
  `kind`, `as_of`, `spine_watermark`, `latest_release {label,
  publication_id}` — additive; absent values are omitted, never fabricated.
  The release-namespaced FTS5 search route
  (`/v1/releases/{pub}/compartments/{comp}/search`, P32.14) is marked
  release-basis too — handler, `SearchIndexError` handler and the route's
  422 path all mark before answering.
- **Service identity (`api/src/api/app.py`)** — `/` and `/health` gain
  `release {label, publication_id, as_of_world}` (from the mounted registry,
  else the `release_id` pin, else `null`), `code_commit` (`SIG_CODE_COMMIT`)
  and `image` (`SIG_IMAGE_DIGEST`) — deploy-set, `None` = not pinned.
- **`sig-api serve` (`api/src/api/cli.py`)** — `--release-registry` now also
  resolves from `SIG_RELEASE_REGISTRY` (Cloud Run sets env, not argv — the
  `ops/gcp/config.sh` `SIG_RELEASE_REGISTRY_DIR` mount path).
- **V7 (`ops/src/ops/release_publish_verify.py`)** — `PF.api_parity` joins the
  promotion preflight: refuses a `sig.api-slice/1` index with the wrong schema
  or foreign `publication_id`, a declared document outside `r/<pub>/api/`,
  unpinned by the integrity manifest, absent on disk, unparseable, or stamped
  with a foreign release; refuses staged dossier pages the slice does not
  cover; refuses api files with no index. A release carrying no slice *and* no
  parity-bound dossier pages records **`deferred`** honestly (owner: the
  release-file toolchain — `D-P35.57-1`; landing: the first candidate cut
  under the contract), never a fabricated pass.
- **Fixture registry** (`tests/api/fixtures/release_registry/`) — two promoted
  publications (`p-aa…` current with a full slice, `p-bb…` a prior promotion
  with a dossier document), catalog/latest/withdrawals, integrity manifests —
  the committed fixture the fixture-verified AC runs against.
- **Tests** — `tests/api/test_api_release_parity.py` (29: both basis classes,
  `?release=` selection, 404 unknown scope still release-labelled, unpromoted
  pub → 404, unpinned/drifted/foreign-stamped bytes fail closed, withdrawal →
  410, `/health` + `/` release identity, honest absence of watermark/registry,
  the search route's release basis); `tests/ops/test_release_publish_verify.py`
  (+8: V7 pass/refuse/deferred matrix).
